root_cause_label: Vision Task Circumvention via OCR Fallback
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose OCR (pytesseract) to analyze a chess board image, a fundamentally unsuitable approach that yielded garbage output, and ultimately fell back to writing a hardcoded generic opening move 'e2e4' unrelated to the actual board position.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: Agent installs opencv-python and pytesseract to perform OCR on the chess board image, committing to an approach that cannot detect or identify chess pieces from a visual board representation.
t_commit_evidence: Step 14 (think): Agent explicitly acknowledges 'OCR isn't suitable for analyzing a visual chess board image' and states 'let me try one more approach - maybe I can find a chess engine and create a simple position to demonstrate the concept, even if it's not the actual position from the image', locking in an ungrounded fallback answer.
t_surface_evidence: Step 13: OCR of the chess board image returns garbage text 'Detected text: ¢ £ WV x / ry & A / ry a ry / a # 2', showing the approach cannot extract board state.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain knowledge that OCR (Optical Character Recognition) is fundamentally incapable of detecting and identifying chess pieces from a visual chess board diagram. The appropriate approach would have been template matching, a vision-capable model, or chess board recognition libraries, not character-based OCR.
forewarning_evidence: Step 13 output shows OCR returning '¢ £ WV x / ry & A / ry a ry / a # 2' - clearly garbage characters that cannot represent a chess board position, visible before t_commit at step 14.
